messages:
Maria: Heads up — saw a weird autoscaler/placement race after we flipped the GPU isolation policy in us-west-2. gpu-pool spun up then nodes immediately went NotReady and some inference pods went Pending.
Ken: Can you paste the last scale event and a pod that's Pending?
sRE-bot: scale-event: added 4 nodes to nodegroup/gpu-pool-usw2 at 2026-03-16T09:03:21Z (reason: target-utilization).
Maria: kubectl snippet: ```
$ kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | egrep "pending|CrashLoop"
inference-serve-abc   0/2   Pending   0   3m   (0s)   -
```
Maria: and node taints: ```
$ kubectl describe node ip-10-0-45-12 | grep -i taint -A2
Taints:    gpu-isolation=true:NoSchedule
```
Oliver: Was the toleration dropped by the helm chart bump? We recently changed chart v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0 and IIRC tolerations moved under podDefaults in the template. :thinking: 
Jo: Yup, saw that. Old deployments had the toleration in podSpec, new helm release is using an outdated values path so the inference chart never got the toleration injected.
Ken: That would cause pods to sit pending until node is drained/gone. But why did nodes go NotReady right after scale-up? Any kubelet errors?
Maria: Nodes show kubelet restarted (OOM on warmup script). The new pool uses smaller instance type for cost reasons and our startup hook downloads model shard — ran out of memory. So kubelet flapped and system taints applied (node.kubernetes.io/not-ready).
Jo: So two simultaneous issues: (1) mis-placed toleration -> pods won't schedule to GPU nodes even when ready, and (2) warmup memory footprint causing node instability. Race: autoscaler sees nodes failing and tries alternate pools -> churn.
Oliver: Short-term mitigation: add a default mutating webhook to inject the gpu toleration for inference namespace, and mark the new nodegroup as unschedulable for non-GPU workloads with taint gpustage=reserved:NoSchedule.
Ken: Also bump the instance type or remove the heavy warmup from node boot — move model shard download to initContainer with ephemeral storage limits and retry, or preload via AMI.
Maria: Agreed. What about fallback routing? Right now when GPU nodes fail, some requests are routed to CPU pool (higher cost latency), but we saw a surge in fallback that spiked billing.
Jo: We should enforce a graceful fallback policy: reject high-CPU requests when there are no GPUs rather than auto-fallback for latency-sensitive endpoints. That reduces unexpected cost.
Ken: Ops tasks: 1) Roll quick patch to helm chart to restore tolerations + push a mutating webhook (low risk) 2) Increase warmup node memory or move to AMI cache 3) Add autoscaler filter to avoid scaling small instance types for gpu-pool during warmup window 4) Add metric alert on fallback-rate > 3%
Maria: I'll open a PR for the helm chart fix and the webhook config. Will also run a smoke test in staging with the smaller instance type to reproduce OOM.
Oliver: I'll change the autoscaler constraints and add a max-unready threshold so it won't keep flapping.
sRE-bot: alert: fallback-rate spike detected 2026-03-16T09:05:14Z -> 11% (inference-service).
Ken: Thanks. Quick note on cost: If we keep the AMI preload approach we pay build time but reduce per-node warmup which saves spot churn. Recommend ROI calc before AMI rollouts.
Maria: Good call. I'll include estimated savings in the PR description.
Jo: tagging @ken for follow-up on alerts and @oliver for autoscaler change. :thumbsup:
Ken: Ack, will take alert owner.
Maria: Thanks team — prioritizing this as P2 until helm patch goes out.
